Picklist values: Direct mail; Cold call; SMS; PPC; SEO; PPL; Driving for dollars; Referral; Other
Why it matters: Without it, no report can tie a contract or a closed deal back to the channel that paid for it.

Required when: Before Status can leave New, when Lead Source is a paid channel
Why it matters: Lead Source says which channel; Campaign says which mailer, list or ad. Spend is entered on the campaign, so cost per appointment and ROI need this link.

Picklist values: Your markets (for example by metro or county)
Why it matters: Lets you compare channels and reps market by market instead of mixing a strong market with a weak one.

Picklist values: New; Attempting Contact; Contacted; Appointment Set; Hot; Warm; Nurture; Under Contract; Dead
Why it matters: One shared list of stages, so a report can count how many leads sit at each step and how long they stay there.

Required when: While the lead is open (Status is not Dead or Under Contract)
Why it matters: An open lead with no next date is a lead nobody is working. This field makes the gap visible and lets you block it.

Required when: Never entered by hand; counted from logged calls, texts and emails to the seller
Why it matters: Shows how much follow-up a lead actually got before it was marked Dead or went under contract.

Required when: Copied from Touch Count when Status changes to Under Contract
Why it matters: Tells you how many touches your deals usually take, so reps stop giving up on leads too early.

Picklist values: Not motivated; Price too high; Listed with agent; Wrong number; Sold; Other
Why it matters: Dead leads with a reason can be revisited at the right time. Dead leads without one are lost for good.

Required when: Set automatically from Dead Reason (see automation-rules.md)
Why it matters: Brings back price-too-high, not-motivated and listed-with-agent leads on a schedule instead of leaving them in a dead pile.

Required when: When Status changes to Appointment Set
Why it matters: Feeds cost per appointment by campaign, the first of the Monday 5.

Required when: Stamped automatically by the first logged outbound call or text to the seller
Why it matters: The timestamp speed to lead is measured from. Created date alone tells you nothing about how fast the team responded.

Required when: Calculated: (First Contact At − lead created time) in minutes
Why it matters: Speed to lead as a number you can average by rep, source and hour of day.

Required when: Set to missed-call time + 5 minutes when an inbound call is missed; cleared when the callback is logged
Why it matters: A missed seller call with a due time can be reported on and escalated. A voicemail nobody sees cannot.
